scope_policy: Start with inspectable scoped interfaces. Structural mathematical recovery and prospective physical calibration are separate classes; no target is an all-physics closure claim.

targets.question: Can the pilot relational source, after declared linearization and spectral enlargement, recover local unitary dynamics and faithful external retained return as an instance of the programme interface?
targets.regime: Finite Bool-factor source; operational completion or declared standard complex semantics; no laboratory time or probability model.
allowed_inputs: native factor maps and source attachment
declared analytic background and uniform spectral rule
targets.success_criterion: Live scoped outcome import at its unchanged verification level plus explicit witness/operation/record transport to this programme source interface.
targets.failure_criterion: A specified transport or required law fails for this pilot; this obstructs this target instance, not every relational carrier.
targets.verification_boundary: Existing operational kernel proof plus accepted written correspondence; programme transport is not yet proved.

targets.question: Does the same realized finite source admit the declared complex-to-real Hamiltonian correspondence with retained return orientation accounted for?
targets.regime: Declared C4 linearization and R8 canonical symplectic realization; dimensionless parameters and given rate/orientation policy.
allowed_inputs: same source instance as the unitary pilot
targets.success_criterion: Explicit same-witness transport and exact identities for the stated generator; distinct scale conventions must be reconciled rather than equated by name.
targets.failure_criterion: A required identity or same-witness/scale transport fails for the stated conventions.
targets.verification_boundary: Reported exact mathematical correspondence; no new formal import or physical energy calibration.

targets.question: Can a source-authorized record map reproduce the complete single-Compton sector probabilities under independently declared preparation and acceptance?
targets.regime: Free unpolarized electron target, unobserved final spin/polarization, fixed incident energy, setting-independent polar support; all no-click records retained.
allowed_inputs: imported Born pairing and Klein-Nishina law
independent preparation and calibrated energy/polar-angle support
required_laws: exhaustive sector sharpness is 2 mu/pi, not mu
for the independently prepared positive eigenstate, p_plus=1/2+mu/pi
settings obtained only by postprocessing one parent record do not give complete-record CHSH above 2
targets.success_criterion: Before data acquisition, freeze the source-instance map, instrument protocol, nuisance model, statistical tolerance and sample rule; compare independent calibration counts to the complete-record prediction.
targets.failure_criterion: Under audited protocol assumptions and the predeclared test rule, held-out records exclude the stated interface; investigate instrument/model assumptions without retroactively fitting acceptance.
targets.verification_boundary: Given physical-theory inputs and a prospective calibration prediction; no acquired counts or established common-carrier realization.
excluded: derivation of QED or Born rule
physical confirmation from ideal analyzer arithmetic

deferred_targets.reason: Missing field phase space, Lorentzian geometry, smearing/constraints and source map; finite covariance and mechanical parametrization do not supply ADM.
Common substrate/preparation, physical port, clock and gain/calibration gates remain open; fitted coefficients are not derived constants.

The old guide's onset/replication receipts are absent at their stated paths, and the proposed single-Compton observed-record promotion is withdrawn. Ideal-amplitude claims require separate evidence recovery and physical analyzer authorization.
Counts and geometric ratios need a physical action, state/preparation, units and readout; no such promotion is made by these pilots.

boundary: Proposed target specification, not approved physical scope, experimental readiness, empirical success or root closure.
